# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 74 (Bu-Vb Pc74)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc74
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 74
**Title (English, from literature):** Hitting in anger
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 74 (known in the tradition under the title *Pahāra*) is an expiation rule (*pācittiya*) belonging to the Suttavibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The rule establishes that a Buddhist monk who, motivated by anger and discontent, gives a blow to or strikes another monk incurs an offense of expiation requiring confession [Horner, Cullavagga]. As noted in studies of comparative monastic law, this rule prohibits monastics from striking a fellow ordained member of the same sex in anger [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 It corresponds to Bhikkhu Pātimokkha Pācittiya 74 and Parivāra Pācittiya 74 in Pali, and aligns with parallel rules in the Sarvāstivāda (Pc 48), Mūlasarvāstivāda (Pc 48), Mahīśāsaka (Pc 71), Mahāsāṅghika (Pc 58), and Dharmaguptaka (Pc 78) recensions in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan. The corresponding nun's rule appears in the Theravāda as Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 152, which likewise possesses parallels throughout other school codes.
